AgentDock 1.0.3: put the dots where you want them, questions that pop up, finish notifications, and agents grouped by repository.

  • Position (Settings › General): keep the dots on the right edge, move them to the left edge, rest them on the Dock (beside it when your Dock is on a side), or wrap them around the notch on a MacBook, where they open into the card below the menu bar. "Only in the Dock" hides the strip.
  • Show in the Dock: AgentDock can also have a Dock icon, with a badge for the agents that need you and their dots drawn on it. Click it for the Inbox; right-click it for every agent. Being in the Dock also puts AgentDock in ⌘-Tab, so it's off unless you turn it on.
  • Decision pop-up (Settings › Inbox, off unless you turn it on): when an agent asks something, its question pops up in the middle of the screen, or drops from the top (out of the notch on a MacBook), until you answer or dismiss it. It never takes your keyboard unless you ask, with ⌃⌥I or a click, or you can let it take the keys a second after it appears. Answers wait two seconds, as in the Inbox, so esc undoes.
  • When an agent finishes (Settings › Inbox): a notification with its last words, after turns longer than you choose, as a macOS notification (follows Focus, waits in Notification Center) or a banner from the top center (out of the notch on a MacBook). Reply right in it, or Show to open its card. It stays quiet while you're looking at that agent, and the dots can flash, the Dock icon bounce or a sound play. Notifications are off unless you turn them on.
  • Group by repository (Settings › Appearance, off unless you turn it on): agents working in one repository, its worktrees included, sit together under its name in the hover card, and their dots share a capsule. Each group sits where its most urgent agent would, so what needs you still comes first, and inside a group every agent shows just its branch.
  • Settings has an Inbox tab, and is a little taller, so every option fits without scrolling.

AgentDock 1.0.2: git branches, macOS 15, Grok Build, and Codex in every terminal.

  • Git branches: every agent shows the branch it's on, so several sessions on one repository tell themselves apart. A git worktree goes by its repository's name ("shop-web ⎇ feature/login" instead of a generated folder name), and ⌥⌥ finds an agent by its branch too ("login: run the tests"). Settings › Appearance › Git branch turns it off.
  • Runs on macOS 15 Sequoia and later. Liquid Glass and the on-device recaps still need macOS 26: on 15 the panels use a frosted blur, and Settings says why recaps are off.
  • Grok Build: Grok runs Claude Code's hook, so with the hook on (Settings › Agents) its sessions show up as Grok, with Grok's logo, in any terminal, cmux and herdr. Its permission prompts can be answered from the Inbox. Until now they showed up labelled as Claude.
  • Codex in a terminal: ⌥⌥ messages and Inbox answers reach the Codex CLI in iTerm, WezTerm, kitty, tmux and herdr. ⌥⌥ took Codex's empty prompt for unsent text, messages could stay in its input without being sent, and AgentDock couldn't type to Codex in iTerm at all.
  • Codex in cmux: when Codex asks for approval, its dot turns amber. It used to stay blue.

Tested end to end with real agents: Claude Code in cmux, tmux, herdr, iTerm, WezTerm, kitty, Terminal, Ghostty, Warp, VS Code and the Claude app; Codex in cmux, tmux, herdr, iTerm, WezTerm and kitty; Grok Build in cmux, tmux, herdr, iTerm and Ghostty.

AgentDock 1.0.1: fixes from testing every terminal with real agents.

  • iTerm: ⌥⌥ messages and Inbox replies are sent again. They were typed into the agent's input but never submitted.
  • kitty: clicking an agent brings its own window forward, not just kitty. Messages with backslashes (a path like C:\temp) arrive exactly as typed.
  • herdr: questions from agents in herdr can be answered from the Inbox again; newer herdr versions wouldn't show a waiting agent's screen. An agent that appeared before herdr recognised it no longer stays without its name and logo.
  • Claude Code in a terminal opened from the Claude app now shows as that terminal instead of "Claude app", so ⌥⌥ can type to it and clicking finds its tab.
  • When an agent has unsent text in its prompt, AgentDock now says to clear it there, instead of always saying "in cmux".

Tested end to end with Claude Code in cmux, tmux, herdr, iTerm, WezTerm, kitty, Terminal and Ghostty.

AgentDock 1.0: now $19, after a 7-day free trial.

  • Try everything for 7 days. After the trial, the status dots and the hover card keep working for free. Answering from the Inbox, ⌥⌥ messages and answering from your iPhone need a license.
  • $19 once (plus tax where it applies), for up to 3 Macs. Buy it from the menu or Settings › License. After paying, your browser brings you straight back to AgentDock with the key filled in.
  • Lost your key? agentdockapp.com/activate finds it again from your email and the card you paid with.
  • Settings › License shows your trial, your license, and frees a Mac when you move to a new one.
  • The iPhone page says when answering is locked, instead of quietly doing nothing.
  • Fixed: two copies of AgentDock running at once (say, a test build) could cut each other off from Claude Code's hook.

Thank you for trying AgentDock early.
